name: Economics Major, B.A.
verified_by: PreReqPath review (AI-assisted, Claude) against the live catalog page; not an official UNC review
notes: Program total: 30-31 hours, depending on the calculus course chosen.
Page also states: final cumulative GPA 2.000; 45 UNC hours; at least half of major core (courses and hours) at UNC; major-core GPA 2.000.
An economics major may apply as many as 15 economics courses, or 45 hours, toward the B.A. degree (the B.A. 45-hour subject cap, applied by the planner).
MATH 231 is recommended for students who plan to take the calculus sequence; MATH 116 is not acceptable.
Footnote 2: the calculus course is a prerequisite for both ECON 400 and ECON 410; ECON 400 and 410 are prerequisites for economics courses numbered above 420.

requirements.label: Gateway Course
notes: Interpretation: the page lists the gateway course separately from the Core Requirements, so it is treated as outside the major core for core GPA, residency, and overlap calculations.

children.label: Four ECON courses at the 400, 500, or 600 level, at least one numbered 500 or higher
children.source_text: Four ECON courses at the 400, 500, or 600 level, with at least one course numbered ECON 500 or higher. 1,3 | 12 || 1 Note that 200- and 300-level courses do not count toward the major. ECON 493 does not count for 400-level credit. ECON 698 will count for 400-level credit only if ECON 384 has been taken; ECON 698 alone will not count toward the major in economics. || 3 Students may not receive credit for both ECON 470 and ECON 570.
notes: Encoded as one ECON course numbered 500-699 plus three more ECON courses numbered 400-699; a course can fill only one slot, so this is exactly four courses with at least one at 500+.
ECON 400, 410 and 420 fill the core slots above and cannot also count here (no double counting within the major).
Footnote 1: ECON 493 is excluded. ECON 698 counts only if ECON 384 has been taken; the planner does not evaluate that condition, so it conservatively excludes ECON 698.
Footnote 3: the planner never schedules both ECON 470 and ECON 570. (ECON 570 is not in the 2026-2027 course listings, so this matters only if it was taken earlier.)
Variable-credit research/independent study and honors courses count when completed but are not auto-selected.
